title: The Best Superwhisper Alternatives in 2026
summary: The best Superwhisper alternatives in 2026, compared honestly on accuracy, offline privacy, price, and platforms so you can pick the right dictation app.
body_markdown:
Superwhisper won a lot of people over by doing something most dictation apps would not: keeping your voice on your own machine. Local Whisper models, custom modes, no audio leaving the device. That is a real feature, and if privacy is your line in the sand, it is a good tool. So this is not a takedown. It is a straight answer to a real question: if Superwhisper is not quite the fit, what should you try next, and why?


**The short answer:** the strongest Superwhisper alternatives in 2026 are Aqua Voice (best accuracy and live, editable text), VoiceInk (best open source, fully local), Spokenly (best free local option with the widest platform support), Wispr Flow (most polished cloud dictation), and MacWhisper (best for transcribing audio files). The right pick depends on whether you value accuracy, offline privacy, price, or platform coverage.


## Why people look for a Superwhisper alternative


Superwhisper is a capable app, so the reasons to switch are usually specific, not "it is bad." The five that come up most:


- **Setup and model management.** Superwhisper asks you to pick models, download them, and configure modes. That flexibility is the point for some people and friction for others who just want to install it and talk.
- **Accuracy on hard words.** Local Whisper models are only as good as the model you load and the machine you run it on. On names, code, medical or legal terms, and product jargon, a tuned model can pull ahead of a general local build.
- **Live feedback and editing.** Superwhisper records, then inserts. Some writers want to watch text appear as they speak, and to fix it by voice without touching the keyboard.
- **Platform coverage.** The Mac app is the flagship and the most mature. The Windows and iOS versions are newer and more limited, and there is no Linux app.
- **Price.** The free tier runs the small local models, but the one-time lifetime license sits near $250 at the time of writing, which is a big upfront ask if you are not sure it is your forever tool.


Match your reason to the list below and the choice gets easy.


## 1. Aqua Voice, best for accuracy and live editable text


We build Aqua Voice, so treat this section as informed rather than neutral, and judge the checkable claims for yourself.


Aqua runs on its own proprietary speech model,[Avalon](https://aquavoice.com/avalon-api) , rather than a general local build you have to download and tune. At its debut on the OpenASR leaderboard in October 2025, Avalon ranked as the top proprietary model (it now sits sixth overall as newer open models have landed). On the AISpeak benchmark Aqua reports 97.3% accuracy, a self-reported figure, so weigh it as one data point. For an independent read, 9to5Mac ran the same passage through Apple Dictation and Aqua and counted 17 errors versus 1.


Two things set the experience apart from Superwhisper's record-and-insert flow. Text appears live as you speak, so you watch it land instead of waiting for a finished block. And Edit Mode lets you revise by voice ("change 'meeting' to 'deadline'", "delete the last sentence") without reaching for the keyboard. Final text lands in about 450ms, and you can dictate up to 230 words per minute.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, iPhone.
- **Languages:** 49.
- **Price:** Free for 1,000 words (a lifetime allowance, not a timed trial), then Pro at $8/mo billed annually. No model downloads, no lifetime license to gamble on.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Aqua processes dictation in the cloud. If your hard requirement is that audio never leaves your device, one of the fully local picks below is the better call.


New to dictation entirely? Our[setup guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) walks through getting comfortable.


## 2. VoiceInk, best open source and fully local


If what you loved about Superwhisper was the offline, on-device processing, VoiceInk is the closest alternative in spirit. It is GPL-licensed, runs speech recognition locally through whisper.cpp, and you can build it from source for free or buy a prebuilt binary to skip the compile. Nothing leaves your machine, and you can audit exactly what it does, which Superwhisper's closed app cannot offer.


- **Platforms:** Mac (source build or paid binary).
- **Price at the time of writing:** free if you build it yourself, a one-time license for the packaged app.
- **The honest tradeoff:** open source means you are your own support desk, and, as with Superwhisper, local accuracy depends on the model and hardware you bring.


## 3. Spokenly, best free local option with the widest platform coverage


Spokenly is the pick if Superwhisper's platform gaps are your issue. It runs local Parakeet and Whisper models on Mac, Windows, Linux, and iPhone, and the on-device models are free with no word caps or trial clock. You can also connect cloud engines with your own API keys, or move to its Pro tier. For anyone who wanted Superwhisper on Linux, or found the Windows build too limited, this is the most direct answer.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone.
- **Price at the time of writing:** free forever for the local models, with a Pro subscription around $10/mo for premium cloud providers and the iOS keyboard.
- **The honest tradeoff:** it is a younger product than the Mac stalwarts, so the polish is still filling in, and local accuracy again tracks the model and machine you use.


## 4. Wispr Flow, best polished cloud dictation


If you are willing to trade offline processing for a smoother, flowing experience, Wispr Flow is the best-known option. It puts a fast, clean-up-as-you-go voice layer across every app, and once you have talked your way through an email instead of typing it, going back feels slow. It is the opposite bet from Superwhisper: cloud instead of local, polish instead of configurability.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, iPhone.
- **Price at the time of writing:** a paid Pro plan roughly in the $12 to $15 per month range, with a capped free tier. Wispr does not publicly disclose the speech model behind it.
- **The honest tradeoff:** it processes speech in the cloud, so it is not an option if local-only is your requirement, and Pro costs more than Superwhisper's monthly plan. For a closer look, we keep a running[Aqua Voice vs Wispr Flow](https://aquavoice.com/vs/wispr-flow) page.


## 5. MacWhisper, best for transcribing audio files


MacWhisper is a slightly different tool for a related job. It is a Mac app built openly on OpenAI's Whisper models (its own listing says so) that shines at turning recordings, meetings, and voice memos into text, with system-wide dictation added on top. If a chunk of your work is transcribing existing audio rather than live dictation, it is the cleanest fit here, and it shares Superwhisper's local, Whisper-based DNA.


- **Platforms:** Mac only.
- **Price at the time of writing:** a free tier for smaller models, with a one-time Pro license for the larger models and features.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Mac only, and file transcription is the center of gravity, so live dictation is not as polished as the dedicated dictation tools.


## A note on meeting tools like Otter.ai


If you landed here but what you actually want is meeting notes, speaker labels, and searchable transcripts, a dictation app is the wrong category. Tools like Otter.ai are built for capturing conversations, not for typing by voice across every app. Worth knowing before you switch, because the two jobs pull in different directions.


## How to choose in one minute


- **You want the most accurate dictation and to see and edit text by voice:** Aqua Voice.
- **Your top requirement is that audio never leaves your device:** VoiceInk or Spokenly.
- **You need Windows or Linux coverage, for free:** Spokenly.
- **You want a polished, flowing cloud experience:** Wispr Flow.
- **You mostly transcribe recordings on a Mac:** MacWhisper.


The honest truth is that most people cannot feel the difference between two decent dictation apps until the words get hard: a colleague's name, a function signature, a drug or a statute. Local models can get you privacy, but accuracy on those words swings with the model and the machine. That is where a purpose-built model earns its keep, and it is the bar we built Aqua to clear. You can[try Aqua free](https://aquavoice.com/) on your next email before you decide.


## FAQ


**What is the best free Superwhisper alternative?**


Spokenly runs local models free forever with no word caps, and VoiceInk is free if you build it from source. Aqua Voice includes 1,000 words free as a lifetime allowance (not a timed trial), and MacWhisper offers a limited free tier before a one-time upgrade.


**What is the best offline alternative to Superwhisper?**


VoiceInk and Spokenly both process speech locally on your device, so no audio is sent to the cloud. VoiceInk is open source and Mac only; Spokenly adds Windows, Linux, and iPhone while keeping a free local tier.


**Is there a Superwhisper alternative for Windows or Linux?**


Yes. Spokenly runs on Mac, Windows, Linux, and iPhone. Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow both cover Mac and Windows, with Aqua adding iPhone. Superwhisper's own Windows and iOS apps exist but are newer and more limited than its Mac app.


**Which Superwhisper alternative is the most accurate?**


Aqua Voice runs on its proprietary Avalon model, which ranked as the top proprietary model at its October 2025 OpenASR debut, and beat Apple Dictation 17 errors to 1 in a 9to5Mac test. Local-model tools like Superwhisper, VoiceInk, and Spokenly vary in accuracy depending on the specific model and hardware you run.
